title: Economic Takeaways From the Trump-Xi Summit and Why It Matters for New Zealand
gist: ASPI's Jane Mellsop argues the Trump-Xi summit in Washington produced mostly process gains (a short trade-truce extension, a new AI dialogue, and a Board of Trade framework) branded as 'constructive strategic stability'. Chip-export and rare-earth-magnet tensions still threaten the fragile truce, which matters greatly for export-dependent New Zealand.

insights.claim: The Trump-Xi summit in Washington was short on substance but was celebrated by both sides as confirming a relationship of 'constructive strategic stability' between the US and China.
insights.so_what: Headline stability may overstate the durability of US-China de-escalation.
insights.quote: was short on substance but was nevertheless celebrated by both sides as confirming a relationship of 'constructive strategic stability' between the US and China
insights.locator: Last week's meeting of the leaders
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute

insights.claim: The Trump-Xi summit delivered a short extension to the US-China trade truce, the launch of a new AI dialogue, and agreement on the framework and mandate for a US-China Board of Trade.
insights.so_what: Only a short truce extension means tariff risk resurfaces soon; the Board of Trade and AI dialogue are new channels to watch.
insights.quote: a short extension to the trade truce, the launch of a new AI dialogue, and agreement on the framework and mandate for their Board of Trade
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute

insights.claim: Tensions over chip exports and access to rare-earth magnets continue to bubble beneath the surface and threaten the fragile US-China trade truce.
insights.so_what: Semiconductor export controls and rare-earth supply remain the most likely triggers for renewed US-China escalation.
insights.quote: tensions around chip exports and access to rare earths magnets continue to bubble just below the surface and threaten the fragile truce
insights.locator: However, the summit delivered largely process gains
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute

insights.claim: Exports make up close to a quarter of New Zealand's GDP, and China and the US are New Zealand's first and second largest export markets.
insights.so_what: New Zealand's economy and currency are highly sensitive to any breakdown in US-China trade relations.
insights.quote: With exports making up close to a quarter of New Zealand's GDP, and China and the US holding first and second place in the list of New Zealand's top export markets
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute

insights.claim: Averting a US-China trade war is critical for New Zealand because its two largest export partners are the two sides of that conflict.
insights.so_what: NZD and NZ exporters are a proxy trade for US-China trade-war risk.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
